newsitem.title: USA: Tenneco Auto sees job cuts, efficiences.
newsitem.headline: Tenneco Auto sees job cuts, efficiences.

text.p: Tenneco Automotive said it expects its shed several hundred positions as part of a restructuring announced Tuesday, bringing to about 1,000 the number of total jobs that will be eliminated.
In a conference call with reporters, Tenneco Automotive President Thomas Evans said the company will first rely on attrition to thin its employee ranks.

Tenneco Automotive, a unit of Tenneco Inc, reorganized its worldwide businesses into six units aimed at eliminating structural costs, boosting operating speed and improving management accountability and customer service.
Previously, many of the company's operating units had their own management structures that reported into an umbrella organization at Tenneco Automotive's headquarters in Deerfield.

Evans declined to specify savings from the move, but he said it is in the "tens of millions of dollars." The savings are part of Tenneco Inc's previously disclosed plan to slash $100 million over the next 18 months.

Tenneco Automotive, which has about 22,000 employees worldwide, had already taken restructuring actions in Europe that will cut 500 to 600 jobs. Much of the new savings is coming from the elimination of management ranks, said Evans.
"The key is there will be a lot of potential cost to take out on the management side," he said.

Evans said Tenneco does not expect to take charges related to the reorganization because of previously recorded reserves of about $65 million at its Walker Manufacturing and Monroe Auto Equipment units.

As part of the reorganization, Tenneco Automotive will relocate its headquarters to the Chicago suburb of Lake Forest, Ill. The new structure will make it easier for the company to continue its strategy of making acquisitions that relate to its existing businesses.
Tenneco Automotive, a major supplier of ride-control and exhaust systems to the auto industry, reported 1996 income of $313 million on revenues of $3 billion.
